# V5 implementation verification

Verified locally on 2026-09-12 on Windows with Node.js 26.7.0 and npm 11.19.0. The work is on `feature/AER0005`, based directly on released v3.1.1 commit `c1353c7993b4ff78e09963b01207d8b2d2c5d29e`. The rejected v4 branch remains unchanged at `af7803f21629e71f3b65036923fffd34277e8b0a`. This is an unreleased working-tree result, not a published package or model efficacy study.

The counts and measurements below describe the initial v5 implementation. Subsequent UI delivery changes and their validation are recorded in [UI interaction delivery](5.0.0-ui-interaction-delivery.md); the original measurements remain historical observations.

## Initial release gate

The final sequential `npm run release:check` exited successfully:

| Check | Observed result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm test` | 60 passed; no failures, skips, cancellations or TODOs | Builder, source/public-content validators, CLI, installer lifecycle, diagnostic contracts, guidance invariants and hardening regressions |
| `npm run validate` | Passed | Public-path check, 90 source files, regenerated distributions identical to an independent fresh build, host contracts and 38 load plans |
| `npm run validate:research` | 5 tests passed; corpus and load validation passed | 26 directives, 6 scenarios, all 110 grievance owners, 37 frozen files, policy closure, official-source/expiry records and 38 load plans |
| `npm run test:packed` | Passed | Real local package creation and isolated global installation; 96-file payload, actual CLI invocation, both-host initialization and doctor, update/uninstall previews |
| Final repository inspection | Passed | Tracked and authored untracked changes, generated/runtime inventory, preserved historical bytes, branch ancestry and whitespace |

Permanent regressions added or revised protect real boundaries: explicit diagnostic selection and status propagation, packed/installed threshold lookup, runtime placement and collision preflight, physical source budgets, frozen metadata-and-data mutation, optional routing and complete fork accounting. They do not claim to measure a model following prose. Existing ownership, locking, recovery, input/error, diagnostic and packaging checks were retained and run.

## Instruction measurements

The complete source kernel is 45 physical lines and 5,120 UTF-8 bytes, including metadata and blank lines. It meets both configured ceilings; its byte budget is full, so additions require a compensating trim.

| Measured load | Estimated tokens, including representative catalog |
| --- | ---: |
| Claude generated base with standard profile | 1,980 |
| Codex generated base with standard profile and all context pointers | 1,968 |
| Largest Claude profile, all route pointers and largest selected skill | 2,652 |
| Largest complete Claude review fork, including skill and agent prompts and possible route pointers | 3,454 |

Automatic base and selected-task ceilings remain 2,000 and 3,500 respectively. Optional cumulative full-reference readings are reported separately at 14,062 tokens for Claude, 13,803 for Codex and 14,864 for the Claude review fork, before adding the representative catalog. No scenario requires reading that entire reference collection.

## Actual v3 upgrade and removal

A separate temporary repository used the actual v3.1.1 archive and CLI, not a synthetic version label. The annotated tag peeled to the source commit above. Both hosts were installed with different profiles: Claude `prototype`, Codex `high-assurance`.

V5 update exited successfully, preserved both profiles and consumer files, and added the diagnostic wrapper, threshold helper and configuration to managed ownership. Installed contrast and size checks exited successfully from the consumer directory. Doctor reported both hosts current.

V5 uninstall exited successfully, removed 56 owned files, restored both host roots, and removed its ledger. All eight consumer files remained byte-exact: the original `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/config.toml`, a consumer reference, a custom Claude rule, a custom Codex skill and the exercised source file. Sampled managed runtime, configuration, profile, reference, skill and agent files were absent. Cleanup verified that every temporary path was contained in the unique fixture root before removing it.

The detailed temporary fixture was removed after verification. This record summarizes the observed assertions; the permanent lifecycle and packed tests remain executable evidence for their respective scopes.

## Failures diagnosed during integration

- Mandatory inherited route reads exceeded the load budget. The product was changed to conditional reference indexes; automatic catalog content, overlapping route pointers and the complete fork task prompt are counted. The limits were not increased.
- A lifecycle fixture changed a heading that no longer existed after the kernel moved first. The staged upgrade now uses a stable fixture marker; the tamper case targets the managed block boundary. The affected lifecycle check and final full gate passed after repair.
- An orchestrator ran research load inspection concurrently with distribution regeneration, causing a missing-file error. Those operations depend on one another; the sequential research check and final release gate passed.
- The migration probe initially ran a relative size check from the repository directory and correctly reported a missing file. It passed from the installed consumer directory. This was an invocation error, not a successful first attempt or a product defect.

These failed attempts are not passing evidence. Only the repaired, correctly scoped runs support the results above.

## Limits

No paid evaluation, live host-adherence study, efficacy comparison, publication, merge or commit was performed. Linux and Node.js 24 CI jobs are configured but were not executed in this local session. Documentation was checked against current official sources; it does not prove host behavior.

Token measurements use the declared UTF-8 byte estimator and a representative catalog path. User/host context, tool wrappers and target paths vary. Optional reference accumulation is reported separately; it is not hidden inside an automatic-load claim or evidence of reduced real task cost.
